application of positive isolation devices and personal locks

facts.site: Marrindal Concentrator and Hydrocarbon Transfer Facility
facts.title: electrical release during start-up after maintenance on TX-3002

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was medical treatment injury, with 1 person injured.

defences.finding: Control ENERGY_SOURCE_IDENTIFICATION: the identification of every energy source for the task was not in place, and the root cause analysis classified this as a task or environmental condition.
Control POSITIVE_ISOLATION_APPLICATION: the application of positive isolation devices and personal locks was not in place, and the root cause analysis classified this as an organisational factor.

Control STORED_ENERGY_DISSIPATION: the dissipation or restraint of trapped and residual energy was never verified as effective, and the root cause analysis classified this as a task or environmental condition.
Control ZERO_ENERGY_VERIFICATION: the proving zero energy before intrusive work was not in place, and the root cause analysis classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the proving zero energy before intrusive work on TX-3002 and record the field verification before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in planning and permitting an isolation, specifically authorising a group isolation. TX-3002 (switchgear and transformers) is in service for plant HV/LV distribution. The task proceeded during start-up after maintenance while the identification of every energy source for the task was not in place. The electrical energy involved is held as HV switchgear, and the recorded presentation was shock, arc flash, unplanned energisation.
response.summary: On 3 December 2013 an incident occurred on TX-3002 at Marrindal Concentrator and Hydrocarbon Transfer Facility during start-up after maintenance, releasing electrical energy held as HV switchgear.
